title: Rabbit or Duck
cn: 第 15 集 · 兔子还是鸭子
novel:
The gang stared at an [[optical|optical]] [[illusion|illusion]]. Some saw a rabbit. Others saw a duck. A long [[debate|debate]] followed, and no one would [[concede|concede]].

"It's obviously a duck," Barney said.

"You're [[blind|blind]]," Robin shot back. "It's a rabbit."

Ted and Marshall, meanwhile, fought over a phone number a woman had left at the bar. Both [[claimed|claim]] it. Both [[insisted|insist]] she had smiled at him.

Barney [[proposed|propose]] a solution: whoever solved the rabbit-or-duck puzzle first would get the number.

Hours passed. Coffee grew cold. Lily [[yawned|yawn]]. No one could agree.

Finally Ted laughed. "We're [[idiots|idiot]]," he said. "The number is for neither of us. She left it for the bartender."

The gang fell silent, then burst into laughter. Some [[arguments|argument]], Ted decided, were never about the prize. They were about the [[thrill|thrill]] of being right — even when you weren't.

optical.en: connected with seeing or the eyes

illusion.en: something that seems real but is not

debate.en: a discussion where people argue different sides

concede.en: to admit that you have lost

blind.en: unable to see; unable to notice

claim.en: to say that something is yours or true

insist.en: to say firmly that something is true

propose.en: to suggest a plan or idea

yawn.en: to open your mouth wide when tired
